title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 9 (Promises, express and implied)

content.overview: Section 9 provides that in so far as the proposal or acceptance of any promise is made in words, the promise is said to be express. In so far as such proposal or acceptance is made otherwise than in words, the promise is said to be implied.
content.glance: Express promise — in words; implied promise — otherwise than in words.
content.study: Where the proposal or acceptance of a promise is made in words, the promise is express. Where it is made otherwise than in words, the promise is implied. Section 9 classifies promises by the mode of communication of proposal or acceptance. Current-law framing: identify whether proposal/acceptance was in words or by conduct; classify as express or implied; then apply formation rules (ss. 3–8, 10).

sections.heading: Express promise
sections.body: Proposal or acceptance made in words — the promise is express.

sections.heading: Implied promise
sections.body: Proposal or acceptance made otherwise than in words — the promise is implied.

examples.title: Implied by conduct
examples.body: A boards a bus and takes a seat. The proposal and acceptance of carriage for fare may be implied otherwise than in words under s. 9.

hypotheticals.question: Can a promise exist without spoken or written words?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 9 recognises implied promises where proposal or acceptance is made otherwise than in words.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-9
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Only written or spoken promises are recognised under the Act.
misconceptions.correction: Section 9 expressly recognises implied promises made otherwise than in words.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 9 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify proposal/acceptance. II. Test whether made in words or otherwise. III. Classify as express or implied. IV. Conclude.
